description: Curated sample questions for the LINA chat UI. Each question is keyed for stable referencing, tagged with which backend(s) it exercises, and annotated with which worker template(s) the supervisor is expected to call. The UI can use `category` to group questions, `backends` for visual badges, and `expected_templates` to highlight cross-system reasoning.
seed_data_assumption: Questions assume the standard sandbox seed (named entities + Faker bulk) is loaded. Named anchors used in queries: matter_acme_v_beta, matter_acme_privacy_review, matter_acme_employment_2023, vendor_walker, vendor_jones, vendor_meridian, tk_walker_partner, tk_walker_associate, tk_jones_partner, tk_meridian_partner, tk_meridian_paralegal, user_jane_smith, user_alex_lee, user_sam_rodriguez.

categories.single_database: Hits exactly one backend; useful for demonstrating a single subsystem in isolation.
categories.multi_database: Requires the supervisor to chain at least two worker calls across different backends and synthesize a combined answer.

questions.text: What is the practice area, status, open date, and budget for matter matter_acme_v_beta?
questions.notes: Most direct Redshift-only query. Verifies vw_matter_current is reachable and matter_lookup template returns expected fields.

questions.text: Show me the total approved spend, invoice count, and budget utilization for matter matter_acme_v_beta in 2024-Q4.
questions.notes: Exercises the materialized view mv_matter_spend_summary with explicit matter_id and fiscal_period filters.

questions.text: What is user_jane_smith's job title, department, and email?
Walk the reporting chain upward from user_alex_lee. Who is their manager, and who is their manager's manager?
questions.notes: Multi-hop within a single backend (manager_chain template loops via manager_user_id). Tests A's special multi-hop template.

questions.text: Show me the partner-level lawyers at Walker & Associates LLP, including their bar admissions and standard hourly rate.
questions.notes: Filters vendor_lawyer_profiles_v1 by vendor_name and timekeeper_classification=Partner.

questions.text: Which outside counsel lawyers in our network specialize in privacy or data-protection work? Give me their names, firms, and jurisdictions.
questions.notes: Full-text match against expertise_summary. Showcases OpenSearch's text scoring vs Redshift's structured filters.

questions.text: Look up the matter whose internal matter_id is matter_acme_v_beta. Tell me its name, status, the budget, plus the owner's full name, email, and department.
questions.notes: Canonical 2-step chain: Redshift returns matter_owner_user_id, OpenSearch resolves it to a real user record. Smallest non-trivial multi-system query — good demo opener.

questions.text: How much has vendor_walker billed on matter_acme_v_beta in 2024-Q4, and who is the senior partner from that firm leading the engagement?
questions.notes: Combines spend analytics from Redshift with timekeeper profile from OpenSearch B. Tests B-↔-C parity (vendor_walker is the same ID in both stores).

questions.text: On the Acme v. Beta litigation last quarter, list each Walker timekeeper who billed time, their billed hours, the rate they billed at, and their standard rate from the firm directory. Flag anyone whose billed rate is more than 5% above the standard.
questions.notes: Heavy multi-step — Redshift returns billed/approved rates per timekeeper, OpenSearch supplies the standard hourly_rate from the profile. The supervisor must compute the variance flag in synthesis.

questions.text: Which three open matters in our portfolio have the highest total approved spend? For each, give me the matter name, total spend, and the full name and department of the matter owner.
questions.notes: Aggregation in Redshift + cross-store join in OpenSearch A. The supervisor needs to resolve N owner_user_ids — a fan-out batched call worth observing.

questions.text: Who at our outside counsel firms has both privacy and litigation experience and has actually billed on any of our active matters in the last quarter? Show me their name, firm, practice areas, and hours billed.
questions.notes: Three-step chain: OpenSearch finds candidate timekeepers by expertise, Redshift checks who actually billed time, OpenSearch enriches the survivors. Stress test for routing — the order of tool calls matters.

questions.text: List the senior counsel members of our Legal department, then for each one show how many open matters they own and the total approved spend on those matters this fiscal year.
questions.notes: Starts from OpenSearch (filter users by job_title + department), then for each user fans out into Redshift to count and sum. Good showcase for fan-out and grouping.
